chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, who said:

Abu Maryam al-Ansari mentioned that al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah urinated one day and did not wash his penis deliberately. So I mentioned that to Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, and he said: What he did was evil. He must wash his penis and repeat his salat, but he does not repeat his wudu (ablution).

key_terms.بِئْسَ مَا صَنَعَ: what he did was evil, expressing strong disapproval of the action
key_terms.ذَكَرَهُ: his penis, referring to the organ that must be washed after urination
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer), which must be repeated in this case
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّدًا: deliberately, indicating the act was done intentionally
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: his wudu (ablution), which does not need to be repeated according to the hadith
key_terms.يَغْسِلَ: to wash, referring here to cleansing the penis

ai.seo_question: If someone urinates and does not wash the penis, must he repeat his salat and wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity after urination. It states that deliberately leaving the penis unwashed requires washing the organ and repeating the salat, but it does not require repeating the wudu (ablution).
